nate_product: OK team — finalizing the PRD for Dedicated Capacity launch. Need to lock acceptance criteria for SLA/throughput/autoscale and a concrete rollback plan. Customer A expects ~3k rps steady text-gen v1 with p99 < 350ms. Can we list possible edge cases and firm launch cut criteria?

anita_eng: noted. I'll sketch sizing + failure modes. quick Q — 3k rps is peak or sustained?

tara_cs: that's sustained for their busiest region (NA-west) during business hours. Peak bursts hit ~5k for short windows.

sam_pm: we should differentiate "sustained" vs "burst" SLAs in the PRD. Launch acceptance should be for sustained, with documented burst behavior and graceful degradation.

miguel_sre: immediate flags: cold-start latency, KV cache warmup, thundering-herd on cold caches, and noisy neighbors from multi-tenant infra. Also need clear alert thresholds and runbook pages.

anita_eng: rough sizing math: for v1 tokens-per-request ~120, avg latency target 150ms per token on the smol model; to hit 3k rps we need ~36k token/s capacity across pool. With current kernels and batching we're looking at 8-10 dedicated A100-equivalents (depends on quant). I'll add margin for 30% headroom.

ryan_platform: adding to that — autoscale policy must include min pool to cover sustained, rapid-scale for bursts up to 5k but with graceful fallback rules. Propose: min=8 nodes, target=12 nodes, max=18 nodes. Canary window + cold-cache warming on scale-out.

nate_product: good. We need acceptance criteria spelled as pass/fail. Draft suggestion: 1) Sustained throughput: service handles 3k rps for 30m with p95 < 200ms and p99 < 350ms 2) Burst handling: when ramped to 5k rps over 60s, no total error rate > 1% and tail latency < 1s 3) Autoscale: scale-up completes to target capacity within 60s and preserves request success rate > 99% during scale 4) Fallback: on capacity shortfall, traffic is routed to compatible lower-cost model with <5% drop in quality metrics (per eval prompts) 5) Observability: traces, per-route latency, and token-level cost visible in console during tests

sam_pm: add acceptance step for rollbacks: if p99 exceeds 2x target for 10m or error rate > 3% for 5m, automatic rollback to prior model config + alert to oncall. Also manual abort path for prod launch.

miguel_sre: agree on rollback triggers. Also require a canary that exercises edge cases: cold cache, spike generator, auth/failure injection. Canary failure => block rollout.

anita_eng: edge-case list for PRD (will expand): - cold-KV-warmup latency spike - persistent tokenization regression for specific token sets - model OOM when seq length > expected - degraded outputs after quantization fallback - tenant isolation bleed under noisy neighbor

ryan_platform: ops config snippet for acceptance tests (devops-friendly):
```
autoscale:
  min_nodes: 8
  target_nodes: 12
  max_nodes: 18
  scale_up_window: 60s
  cooldown: 90s
  canary_traffic: 5%
  fallback_model: "text-gen-smol-v0.9"
```

nate_product: nice. @jess_legal — any compliance flags if we route traffic to fallback models for enterprise A? They require model provenance logs retained for 90 days.

jess_legal: routing to fallback model is ok as long as we keep per-request provenance (model id, timestamp, customer id) and store logs in their audit bucket. Add an opt-out flag for customers that want no fallback. Also ensure data residency constraints for their EU traffic.

tara_cs: Customer A will likely ask for opt-out. We should include a contractual note in PRD and CS playbook.

miguel_sre: tests we must run pre-launch: long-run soak (24h) at sustained 3k rps, burst stress + 1h soak, canary with failure injection (drop nodes, delayed kernel), and perf regression of p95/p99 vs baseline.

anita_eng: I'll prepare the test harness and perf dashboard. Need test datasets (production-like prompts) from CS. @tara_cs can you get anonymized traffic samples?

tara_cs: on it — will share sanitized request traces and top 100 prompt templates by EOW.

nate_product: acceptance docs should include: runbook, rollback playbook, CS comms, opt-out clause, measurement dashboards, and SLO appendix. Who owns the rollback playbook?

miguel_sre: SRE owns runbook + rollback automation, eng owns safe-fallback code, product + CS own customer comms and contractual opt-outs.

sam_pm: final ask — include explicit performance budget (tokens/sec, cost/unit) so finance can sign off. Also add launch checklist checkbox for security review.

deploy_bot: deploy scheduled: dedicated-capacity/canary -> 2009876600 by @anita_eng. Status: queued. :white_check_mark:

nate_product: thanks. Anita, Miguel, can you sync tomorrow 10am to finalize numbers and acceptance doc? If we get green, we'll schedule a soft-launch canary with Customer A next week.

anita_eng: yes. 10am works. I'll bring draft sizing and test plan.

miguel_sre: I'll bring runbook and alert thresholds.

nate_product: perfect — I'll update PRD with the acceptance criteria above and circulate for sign-off after the sync. Thanks everyone :rocket:
